decisions.statement: A registration lands the token as a `device-token` page through the pages system service.
The person a token is kept against is read from the account the registration signs in under.
A registration naming a contributor is read to a person by that contributor instead.
A registration naming both is read by its contributor.
The app a token is kept against is the iOS app page with the bundle registered.
A registration for a token already kept replaces the page that token was kept on.
The tokens a push is addressed to are read back for the account the push is sent for.
A token whose app no page has refuses the whole read rather than being left out.
A token Apple no longer reaches is removed at the path its page was read at.
No refusal has the token a device presented.
The platform a registration states is not kept.
The sort of push a token takes is kept beside the token.
A registration naming no sort registers a token taking an alert.
A token kept before any sort was named reads back as taking an alert.
Nothing here decides which sort a push is addressed to.
The values a registration writes are the properties the page type declares.
Which page type a page is and which slug it has are said beside its values.
The app a token is kept under is an iOS app.
A token names its person and its app by page type and slug.
The slug a token's page is named by is the person, the app and the token.
Nothing here reaches Apple.
The markdown device token pages the notifier read before are kept and read by nothing.

definition: the push token a device is reached at, kept against whoever has it and read back to reach them
